sections.h2: Where is Miami County, Ohio, and which towns does it include?
sections.html:
Miami County sits in western Ohio as part of the Dayton metropolitan area, with Shelby County to the north, Champaign and Clark counties to the east, Montgomery County to the south and Darke County to the west. The county was founded March 1, 1807 and takes its name from the Miami people. According to Wikipedia it covers 410 square miles, and the auditor's home page counts 54,707 parcels.

Troy holds the courthouse and is the largest city. Piqua and Tipp City are cities too, and parts of Huber Heights and Union reach into the county. Nine public school districts serve the territory: Bethel, Bradford, Covington, Miami East, Milton-Union, Newton, Piqua, Tipp City and Troy. Which district a house falls into changes the levies on its tax bill.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show for Miami County homeowners?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's QuickFacts table counts 112,634 residents in July 2025, 3.5 percent above the 2020 base. The 2020 to 2024 housing figures:

  • Owner-occupied rate: 73.4 percent among 44,906 households.
  • The middle owner-occupied house is valued at $229,100.
  • Median monthly owner cost: $1,453 with a mortgage and $549 without.
  • Median gross rent: $966.
  • Median household income: $76,817.
  • Building permits in 2025: 340, with 47,930 housing units in July 2025.

About one occupied home in four is rented, so a landlord selling a tenant-occupied house in Troy or Piqua is a familiar case.

sections.h2: How does the Miami County Auditor value a house?
sections.html:
The auditor's office states that Ohio law calls for a general reappraisal every six years, with an update at the three-year midpoint, and that taxation is based on 35 percent of fair market value. The office keeps a record of the appraisal on every parcel, open to public inspection. Ask the auditor which year the next reappraisal or update falls in.

The auditor cannot raise or lower the tax itself. Rates come from the budget requests of each local government and the votes of residents, and the tax bill is the rate times the valuation on the general tax list. Ohio law holds unvoted taxation to the 10 mill limitation, or $10.00 per $1,000 of assessed value. Anything above that has to be voted. Special assessments, such as ditch work, street paving, curbs, sidewalks or sewer and water lines, appear as a separate line on the bill.

sections.h2: When are Miami County property taxes due, and what are the penalties?
sections.html:
Real estate tax is collected in two halves. The treasurer's FAQ gives February 14 for the first installment and July 20 for the second, and the printed statement shows the exact dates. An envelope postmarked on the due date counts as on time.

Miami County tax collection dates and penalties, from the treasurer's FAQ
ItemDetail
Real estate, first halfDue February 14
Real estate, second halfDue July 20
Mobile home, first halfDue March 1
Mobile home, second halfDue July 31
Penalty, first ten days late5 percent
Penalty after ten days10 percent on unpaid current tax

The treasurer's office is in the Safety Building at 201 W. Main Street, Troy, and its phone number is (937) 440-6045. Taxes can be paid by mail with the bill stub, in person on weekdays between eight and four, or in the night deposit box on the east side of the building. Card payments run through a separate processor that adds a 2.50 percent fee, and eChecks add a flat $1.99.

Owners who are behind can ask about a delinquent payment contract. Ohio law also allows tax lien certificate sales under section 5721.32 of the Revised Code.

sections.h2: What tax relief can a Miami County homeowner claim?
sections.html:
The auditor's pages describe several programs. Most require an application filed with the auditor.

  • Owner occupancy credit. You must own the home and live in it as your principal residence on January 1 of the year you file. It covers the dwelling and up to one acre, and it is often handled at the time of transfer.
  • Non-business credit. It applies only to residential and agricultural levies that were in place before the November 2013 election.
  • Homestead exemption. Owners 65 or older, or permanently disabled, who live in the home may qualify. The office says applications can be filed from the first Monday in January to the first Monday in June, and new applicants face an income test.
  • Surviving spouse of a public service officer. The auditor describes a $58,000 reduction with no income limit for the spouse of a firefighter, paramedic or peace officer killed in the line of duty.
  • Current agricultural use value. Farmland of ten or more acres in commercial use, or smaller tracts earning an average $2,500 a year, may apply between the first Monday in January and the first Monday in March.

Call the auditor at (937) 440-5925 for the current homestead income limit.

sections.h2: Where does a Miami County owner contest a valuation?
sections.html:
The Board of Revision hears valuation complaints. The auditor serves as its permanent secretary, and the county treasurer and the president of the board of commissioners complete the panel. A property owner files DTE Form 1, the Complaint Against the Valuation of Real Property, with the auditor between January 1 and March 31.

After the board reviews the complaints, the owner is notified of the decision or scheduled for a formal hearing. The Ohio Department of Taxation says an appeal covers the assessed value of the property, not the millage rate, which comes from local governments and voter-approved levies. The state also suggests collecting recent sales of similar homes, an independent appraisal or photographs to support the complaint. An appraisal helps but is not required.

sections.h2: What should owners of Miami County mobile homes and farmland know?
sections.html:
Mobile homes follow their own calendar. The treasurer's FAQ puts the first half due March 1 and the second half July 31. County pages say owners of manufactured homes must register them with the auditor, who assesses each home every year and sends tax bills twice a year. The money is split among townships, cities and schools the same way real estate tax is.

Farmland has a separate path. The auditor's office administers the current agricultural use value program, which the Ohio Department of Taxation oversees and which sets soil rate values for qualifying land. During a reappraisal year the office says applications may be accepted all year. A parcel that leaves agricultural use can see a change in how it is valued, so ask the auditor before you list a farm tract for sale.

sections.h2: What does a Miami County seller pay at transfer?
sections.html:
The auditor's conveyance information sets the fee at $2.00 per thousand dollars of the purchase price, plus a transfer fee of 50 cents per parcel. The check has to match the exact amount or the conveyance will not be processed. A regular sale uses DTE Form 100. A transfer that qualifies for an exemption uses DTE Form 100 (EX). The auditor's site offers a conveyance fee calculator for an estimate.

The county recorder, auditor and engineer adopted conveyance standards together, and the standardization rules of ORC 317.114 have applied to recorded documents since July 1, 2009. Ask the treasurer's office for a payoff figure on current tax before closing, and ask the title company how the tax is prorated. If the buyer will live in the house, the owner occupancy application is often filed as part of the transfer.

faqs.q: When is the second-half real estate tax due in Miami County?
faqs.a: July 20, according to the treasurer's FAQ. The February installment is due on the 14th, and the printed statement carries the exact dates. A payment postmarked on the due date counts as on time.

faqs.q: What is the late penalty on Miami County property tax?
faqs.a: It is 5 percent for the first ten days after the due date and 10 percent after that on unpaid current tax. Delinquent payment contracts are available from the treasurer's office.

faqs.q: When can I file a valuation complaint in Miami County?
faqs.a: Between January 1 and March 31, using DTE Form 1 filed with the county auditor. The Board of Revision then decides the complaint or sets a formal hearing.

faqs.q: What is the Miami County conveyance fee?
faqs.a: The auditor lists $2.00 per thousand dollars of the purchase price plus 50 cents per parcel. The check must be for the exact amount. Use DTE Form 100, or Form 100 (EX) for an exempt transfer.

faqs.q: How do I apply for the homestead exemption in Miami County?
faqs.a: File an application with the county auditor between the first Monday in January and the first Monday in June. You must be 65 or older, or permanently disabled, and live in the home. Call (937) 440-5925 about the income test.
